paras.t: Denique, ad intelligendum plene historiam hujus primi libri, oporteret habere recursum ad librum sequentem, videlicet secundum Machabæorum, ubi eadem recitantur pro magna parte quæ hic, et frequenter cum additione. Nam et de isto puncto habetur libro secundo Machabæorum.
paras.en: Lastly, to understand the history of this first book fully, one would need to have recourse to the following book, namely the second of Machabees, where for the most part the same things are recounted as here, and often with additions. For this point too is treated in the second book of Machabees[[2 Mach 6:11||]] [the margin gives II Mach. vi; the passage that answers to what follows here (vv. 31–38) is 2 Mach 6:11, the Jews burnt in the caves while keeping the sabbath].

paras.t: Et renuntiatum est viris regis, id est ministris ac ducibus Antiochi, qualiter quidam contempsissent præcepta illius, et confugissent ad loca deserti, et abissent post illos multi fideles Judæi. Et statim perrexerunt ad eos viri Antiochi; et concitaverunt adversus eos prælium in die sabbati, scientes quod illa die non repugnarent Judæi. Et non responderunt Judæi eis, hoc est ministris regis: vel quia modicum responderunt, quod reputatur pro nihilo; vel non responderunt ad ultimo interrogata; aut non responderunt ad vota seu voluntatem quærentium. Aliqua tamen verba responderunt, ut patet in littera. Nec oppilaverunt, hoc est non obstruxerunt, loca occulta, per quæ hostes potuerunt eos accedere, ne tantumdem operando sabbatum violarent.
paras.en: [[2:31|And it was told to the king's men|Et renuntiatum est viris regis]], that is, to the officers and captains of Antiochus, how certain men had despised his commands and fled to the places of the desert, [[2:31|and that many were gone after them|et abissent post illos multi]], faithful Jews. [[2:32|And forthwith they went out towards them|Et statim perrexerunt ad eos]], the men of Antiochus; [[2:32|and made war against them on the sabbath day|et concitaverunt adversus eos prælium in die sabbati]] [Denis has *concitaverunt*, the word of v. 35, for *constituerunt*], knowing that on that day the Jews would not resist. [[2:36|But they answered them not|Et non responderunt Judæi eis]], that is, the Jews did not answer the king's officers: either because they answered little, which is counted for nothing; or they did not answer the last thing asked; or they did not answer to the wishes or will of those asking. Yet they did answer some words, as appears in the text. Nor [[2:36|stopped up|oppilaverunt]], that is, did they block, [[2:36|the secret places|loca occulta]] through which the enemy could get at them, lest by doing even so much work they should violate the sabbath.

paras.t: Dicentes: Moriamur omnes in simplicitate nostra, id est in simplici fide, qua juxta superficiem litteræ videtur esse illicitum sabbato præliari, quum scriptum sit: Nihil operis facietis in eo. Et iterum: Maneat unusquisque apud semetipsum. Verumtamen ista simplicitas fuit partim columbina, quia simulatione et duplicitatis caruit plica; et partim, ut apparet, asinina, quia discretione et vera intelligentia præcepti de observantia sabbati, fuit privata. Excusabilis tamen fuit in istis, quoniam (ut videtur) nondum fuit ab Hebræorum doctoribus determinatum, quod in sabbato liceret pugnare: imo adhuc tempore Christi inter Judæos conversantis, ipsi Scribæ et Pharisæi præceptum de sanctificatione sabbati male intelligebant. Unde et Christum de violatione sabbati frequenter reprehenderunt, quibus ille convenienter respondit. Itaque per præceptum de sabbati celebratione, non prohibebantur necessaria ad damna vitanda, ut bovem et asinum solvere, et adaquandum deducere, et minus ea quæ necessaria sunt ad vitæ defensionem, ut præliari aut persecutionem fugere, sicut Elias a facie Jezabel fugiens, ambulavit quadraginta diebus.
paras.en: [[2:37|Saying: Let us all die in our innocency|Dicentes: Moriamur omnes in simplicitate nostra]] [the Latin word, *simplicitas*, is literally *simplicity*], that is, in simple faith, according to which, going by the surface of the letter, it seems unlawful to fight on the sabbath, since it is written: [[Ex 12:16|you shall do no work in them|Nihil operis facietis in eo]]. And again: [[Ex 16:29|let each man stay at home|Maneat unusquisque apud semetipsum]]. Yet this simplicity was partly that of the dove, because it was free of pretence and of the fold of duplicity; and partly, as it appears, that of the ass, because it lacked discretion and a true understanding of the precept about keeping the sabbath. Yet they were excusable in this, since (as it seems) it had not yet been determined by the doctors of the Hebrews that it was lawful to fight on the sabbath: nay, even in the time when Christ lived among the Jews, the Scribes and Pharisees themselves understood the precept of sanctifying the sabbath badly. Hence they often reproached Christ with breaking the sabbath, and he answered them fittingly[[Matt 12:2||]][[Matt 12:10||]][[Mark 2:24||]][[Mark 3:2||]][[Luke 6:3||]][[Luke 13:14||]][[Luke 14:3||]][[John 7:22||]][[John 9:16||]]. Thus the precept of keeping the sabbath did not forbid what is necessary to avoid loss, such as loosing an ox or an ass and leading it to water, and still less what is necessary to defend one's life, such as fighting or fleeing persecution, as Elias, fleeing from the face of Jezabel, walked forty days[[3 Kings 19:8||]].

paras.t: Et testes erunt super nos cælum et terra, id est, cives cælestes et habitantes in terra testabuntur pro nobis coram summi Judicis tribunali, quod injuste perditis, hoc est occiditis, nos. Angeli etenim sancti testantur pro sibi commissis et justis in Dei judicio; et viri perfecti, per modum assessoriæ dignitatis, judicabunt cum Christo et ejus approbabunt sententiam. Hinc ait Propheta de Deo: Advocabit cælum desursum et terram discernere populum suum.
paras.en: And [[2:37|heaven and earth shall be witnesses for us|testes erunt super nos cælum et terra]], that is, the citizens of heaven and the dwellers on earth will bear witness for us before the judgment seat of the supreme Judge, [[2:37|that you put us to death wrongfully|quod injuste perditis]], that is, slay us. For the holy angels bear witness in God's judgment for those committed to them and for the just; and perfect men, in the dignity of assessors, will judge with Christ and approve his sentence. Hence the Prophet says of God: [[Ps 49:4|He shall call heaven from above, and the earth, to judge his people|Advocabit cælum desursum et terram discernere populum suum]].

paras.t: Et intulerunt illis bellum sabbatis; et mortui sunt usque ad mille hominum animas, id est mille supposita speciei humanæ: sicque sumitur pars pro toto, quemadmodum in Actorum libro, Eramus universæ animæ in navi ducentæ septuaginta sex. Ex hoc ergo verbo non sequitur, quod animæ hominum sint mortales.
paras.en: [[2:38|So they gave them battle on the sabbath|Et intulerunt illis bellum sabbatis]]; [[2:38|and they were slain|et mortui sunt]] [[2:38|to the number of a thousand persons|usque ad mille hominum animas]] [the Latin has *a thousand souls of men*], that is, a thousand individuals of the human species [*supposita*: in the language of the schools, individual subsisting beings]: and so the part is taken for the whole, as in the book of Acts: [[Acts 27:37|And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls|Eramus universæ animæ in navi ducentæ septuaginta sex]]. From this word, then, it does not follow that the souls of men are mortal.

paras.t: Et dixit vir proximo suo, hoc est, unus Judæorum residuorum fidelium dixit ad alium: Si non pugnaverimus pro animabus nostris, id est pro defensione vitæ nostræ, et justificationibus, hoc est observationibus legis, et pro conservatione cultus divini, citius disperdent nos de terra, id est, omnes nos trucidabunt, et ita ex erroneo intellectu præcepti de observantia sabbati, sequetur magis inhonoratio Dei et destructio legis, quam conservatio ejus. Et cogitaverunt in die illa, dicentes: Quicumque venerit ad nos, id est contra nos, in bello die sabbatorum, pugnemus contra eum. Hoc determinaverunt ex informatione Mathathiæ, qui fuit peritus in lege, atque ut Josephus refert, dixit: Si sic legem servaveritis, eritis hostes legis, dantes causam ut pereat populus Dei, et lex cum plebe peribit. Et ex tunc inolevit consuetudo Judæis pugnandi in sabbato, si bella consurgant in eo.
paras.en: [[2:40|And every man said to his neighbour|Et dixit vir proximo suo]], that is, one of the faithful Jews who remained said to another: If we do [[2:40|not fight|non pugnaverimus]] [[2:40|for our lives|pro animabus nostris]], that is, for the defence of our life, [[2:40|and our justifications|et justificationibus]], that is, the observances of the law, and for the preservation of the worship of God, [[2:40|they will now quickly root us out of the earth|citius disperdent nos de terra]], that is, they will slaughter us all; and so, from a mistaken understanding of the precept about keeping the sabbath, there will follow dishonour to God and the destruction of the law rather than its preservation. [[2:41|And they determined in that day, saying|Et cogitaverunt in die illa, dicentes]]: [[2:41|Whosoever shall come up against us|Quicumque venerit ad nos]] [the Latin has *to us*; Denis explains, *that is, against us*] [[2:41|to fight on the sabbath day|in bello die sabbatorum]], [[2:41|we will fight against him|pugnemus contra eum]]. This they determined on the instruction of Mathathias, who was skilled in the law and, as Josephus relates, said: If you keep the law in this way, you will be enemies of the law, giving cause for the people of God to perish, and the law will perish with the people. And from then on the custom grew up among the Jews of fighting on the sabbath, if wars arise on it.

paras.t: Tunc congregata est ad eos, puta ad Mathathiam et suos, synagoga, id est collectio Judæorum, fortis viribus corporalibus ac spiritualibus, omnis voluntarius in lege; et omnes qui fugiebant a malis, facti sunt illis ad firmamentum. Et collegerunt exercitum, eligentes sibi Mathathiam in principem, et percusserunt peccatores, tam gentiles quos invenerunt, quam Judæos incredulos ad paganismum conversos, in ira sua per zelum; et ceteri qui eorum manus evaserunt increduli, fugerunt ad nationes.
paras.en: [[2:42|Then was assembled to them|Tunc congregata est ad eos]], that is, to Mathathias and his men, [[2:42|the congregation|synagoga]], that is, the gathering of the Jews, [[2:42|the stoutest|fortis viribus]] [literally *strong in strength*] in strength of body and of spirit, [[2:42|every one that had a good will for the law|omnis voluntarius in lege]]; and [[2:43|all they that fled from the evils|omnes qui fugiebant a malis]] [[2:43|were a support to them|facti sunt illis ad firmamentum]]. [[2:44|And they gathered an army|Et collegerunt exercitum]], choosing Mathathias as their prince, [[2:44|and slew the sinners|et percusserunt peccatores]], both the Gentiles they found and the faithless Jews who had turned to paganism, [[2:44|in their wrath|in ira sua]], through zeal; [[2:44|and the rest|et ceteri]], the faithless who escaped their hands, [[2:44|fled to the nations|fugerunt ad nationes]].

paras.t: Et circuivit Mathathias et amici ejus urbes et valles Judæ, et destruxerunt aras idolis fabricatas, et circumciderunt pueros incircumcisos. In tali etenim casu non oportuit circumcisionem fieri die octavo a nativitate. Et prosperatum est opus in manibus eorum, id est, opera bona quæ inceperunt, Deo auxiliante, expeditum habuerunt successum, prosperumque processum; et obtinuerunt legem de manibus gentium et regum, id est, observantiam legis Mosaicæ recuperaverunt, repulsa infidelium potestate, quæ ad tempus fuit suppeditata; et non dederunt cornu peccatori, id est, sceleratissimo Antiocho non exhibuerunt exaltationem, sed magis depressionem suæ potestatis, quia ea abutebatur ad contumeliam Creatoris. Idcirco in talibus non fuit ei obediendum, sed resistendum.
paras.en: [[2:45|And Mathathias and his friends went round about|Et circuivit Mathathias et amici ejus]] the cities and valleys of Juda, [[2:45|and they threw down the altars|et destruxerunt aras]] built for idols, and [[2:46|they circumcised all the children|circumciderunt pueros]] [[2:46|that were uncircumcised|incircumcisos]]. For in such a case circumcision did not have to be done on the eighth day from birth. And [[2:47|the work prospered in their hands|prosperatum est opus in manibus eorum]], that is, the good works they had begun had, with God's help, a ready success and a prosperous course; and [[2:48|they recovered the law out of the hands of the nations, and out of the hands of the kings|obtinuerunt legem de manibus gentium et regum]], that is, they recovered the observance of the law of Moses, driving back the power of the unbelievers, which had been granted them for a time; [[2:48|and they yielded not the horn to the sinner|et non dederunt cornu peccatori]], that is, they showed the most wicked Antiochus no exaltation, but rather the abasement of his power, because he abused it to the insult of the Creator. Therefore in such things he was not to be obeyed, but resisted.

paras.t: Et appropinquaverunt dies Mathathiæ ut moreretur, et dixit filiis suis: Nunc confortata est superbia, id est, Antiochus superbiam suam jam ad tempus potenter per tyrannicam abusionem exsecutus est, et castigatio, id est, afflictio nobis per ipsum inducta propter nostra peccata, magna fuit et fortis; et tempus eversionis, qua subversa est observantia legis divinæ, roboratum fuit adversus nos. Tempus autem sumit denominationem ab his quæ fiunt in tempore, ut dicatur bonum vel malum, prosperum aut adversum, forte seu debile. Et ira indignationis, id est ultio nostræ transgressionis, nobis inducta ex detestatione divinæ justitiæ, qua nostra delicta detestatus est Deus.
paras.en: [[2:49|Now the days drew near that Mathathias should die|Et appropinquaverunt dies Mathathiæ ut moreretur]], [[2:49|and he said to his sons|et dixit filiis suis]]: [[2:49|Now hath pride|Nunc confortata est superbia]] gotten strength, that is, Antiochus has now for a time carried out his pride mightily through tyrannical abuse, [[2:49|and chastisement|et castigatio]], that is, the affliction brought upon us through him for our sins, has been great and strong; [[2:49|and the time of destruction|et tempus eversionis]], in which the observance of the divine law has been overthrown, has been strengthened against us. Now a time takes its name from the things that are done in time, so that it is called good or bad, prosperous or adverse, strong or weak. And [[2:49|the wrath of indignation|ira indignationis]], that is, the punishment of our transgression, brought upon us by the detestation of the divine justice with which God has detested our sins.

paras.t: Nunc ergo, o filii, æmulatores estote legis, id est, tempore hujus adversitatis tantæ ferventius diligite atque defendite legem, quo acrius impugnatur; et date animas vestras, id est, vitam vestram periculis mortis constanter exponite, pro testamento patrum, id est pro defensione veteris Testamenti patribus nostris dati in monte Sinai, ut in Exodo legitur. Quemadmodum enim quilibet homo pro defensione totius corporis sui exponit manum, seu quodcumque aliud membrum; sic pro defensione boni communis, potissime cultus divini, unusquisque debet se totum exponere.
paras.en: [[2:50|Now, therefore, O my sons, be ye zealous for the law|Nunc ergo, o filii, æmulatores estote legis]], that is, in the time of so great an adversity, love and defend the law the more fervently the more fiercely it is attacked; [[2:50|and give your lives|et date animas vestras]], that is, expose your life steadfastly to the perils of death, [[2:50|for the covenant of your fathers|pro testamento patrum]], that is, for the defence of the Old Testament given to our fathers on Mount Sinai, as is read in Exodus[[Ex 20:1||]]. For as any man exposes his hand, or any other member, for the defence of his whole body; so for the defence of the common good, and above all of the worship of God, each one ought to expose his whole self.

paras.t: Et mementote operum patrum, ut ea sequamini, et accipietis gloriam magnam, id est copiosam a Deo mercedem, et nomen æternum, id est famam laudibus plenam in præsenti et in futuro, juxta illud, In memoria æterna erit justus; et alibi, Memoria justi cum laudibus. Unde secundum Josephum, inter cetera dixit: Corpora quidem mortalia sunt; operum vero justorum monumenta, id est commemorationes, immortalitatis ordinem consequuntur. Ideo bona quæ nullo fine collaudanda sunt, appetatis; et in quo quis melior fuerit altero, cedentes vobis invicem, propriis ministrate virtutibus.
paras.en: [[2:51|And call to remembrance the works of the fathers|Et mementote operum patrum]], so as to follow them, [[2:51|and you shall receive great glory|et accipietis gloriam magnam]], that is, an abundant reward from God, [[2:51|and an everlasting name|et nomen æternum]], that is, a fame full of praises in the present and in the future, according to that, [[Ps 111:7|The just shall be in everlasting remembrance|In memoria æterna erit justus]]; and elsewhere, [[Prov 10:7|The memory of the just is with praises|Memoria justi cum laudibus]]. Hence, according to Josephus, he said among other things: Bodies indeed are mortal; but the monuments of just works, that is, their remembrance, attain the rank of immortality. Therefore seek those goods which are to be praised without end; and in whatever one of you is better than another, yielding to one another, serve with your own virtues.

paras.t: Abraham nonne in tentatione inventus est fidelis? id est, ex fide et fidelitate paratus Deo obedire in immolatione carissimi filii sui Isaac, ut in Genesi narratur; et reputatum est ei ad justitiam, id est, a Deo approbatus est, et justus reputatus pro obedientia illa et voluntate completa. Hinc Jacobus inducit: Abraham pater noster, nonne ex operibus justificatus est, offerens Isaac filium suum super altare?
paras.en: [[2:52|Was not Abraham found faithful in temptation|Abraham nonne in tentatione inventus est fidelis]]? That is, ready through faith and faithfulness to obey God in the sacrifice of his dearest son Isaac, as is told in Genesis[[Gen 22:9||]][[Gen 22:10||]]; [[2:52|and it was reputed to him unto justice|et reputatum est ei ad justitiam]], that is, he was approved by God and reputed just for that obedience and his complete will. Hence James brings in: [[Jas 2:21|Was not Abraham our father justified by works, offering up Isaac his son upon the altar?|Abraham pater noster, nonne ex operibus justificatus est, offerens Isaac filium suum super altare]]

paras.t: Joseph in tempore angustiæ suæ, id est captivitatis servitutisque in Ægypto, custodivit mandatum Dei de adulterio evitando. Mandata namque Decalogi ad naturalem pertinent legem: quæ sunt de judicio naturalis rationis omnibus insito. Propter quod Joseph dixit ad feminam: Quomodo possum hoc malum facere, et peccare in Deum meum? ut scriptum est in Genesi. Et factus est dominus Ægypti, id est præpositus et princeps sub Pharaone, qui dixit ad Joseph, Uno tantum regni solio te præcedam: ut patet in Genesi.
paras.en: [[2:53|Joseph, in the time of his distress|Joseph in tempore angustiæ suæ]], that is, of his captivity and bondage in Egypt, [[2:53|kept the commandment|custodivit mandatum]] of God about shunning adultery. For the commandments of the Decalogue belong to the natural law, being of the judgment of natural reason implanted in all [so that Joseph was bound by them before they were given on Sinai]. Wherefore Joseph said to the woman: [[Gen 39:9|how then can I do this wicked thing, and sin against my God?|Quomodo possum hoc malum facere, et peccare in Deum meum]] as is written in Genesis. And [[2:53|he was made lord of Egypt|factus est dominus Ægypti]], that is, governor and prince under Pharao, who said to Joseph, [[Gen 41:40|only in the kingly throne will I be above thee|Uno tantum regni solio te præcedam]]: as appears in Genesis.

paras.t: Phinees pater noster, de cujus semine nos sacerdotes geniti sumus, zelando zelum Dei, id est, amando et exercendo zelum Deo placentem pro conservando Dei honore et impietate ulciscenda: ex quo zelo (ut tactum est) perfodit turpiter agentes; accepit testamentum sacerdotii æterni, id est pactum seu promissionem, quod sacerdotale officium permaneret ei ac posteris ejus per omne tempus veteris Testamenti, juxta illud Numerorum: Locutus est Dominus ad Moysen: Ecce do ei pacem fœderis mei, et erit tam ei quam semini ejus pactum sacerdotii sempiterni, quia zelatus est pro Deo suo.
paras.en: [[2:54|Phinees, our father|Phinees pater noster]], of whose seed we priests are born, [[2:54|by being fervent in the zeal of God|zelando zelum Dei]], that is, by loving and exercising a zeal pleasing to God, for preserving God's honour and avenging impiety: out of which zeal (as was touched on above) he thrust through those who were doing a shameful thing[[Num 25:8||]]; [[2:54|received the covenant of an everlasting priesthood|accepit testamentum sacerdotii æterni]], that is, the pact or promise that the priestly office would remain to him and his descendants through the whole time of the Old Testament, according to that of Numbers: [[Num 25:10|the Lord said to Moses|Locutus est Dominus ad Moysen]]: [[Num 25:12|behold I give him the peace of my covenant|Ecce do ei pacem fœderis mei]], and [[Num 25:13|the covenant of the priesthood for ever shall be both to him and his seed, because he hath been zealous for his God|et erit tam ei quam semini ejus pactum sacerdotii sempiterni, quia zelatus est pro Deo suo]].

paras.t: Jesus dum implevit verbum, factus est dux Israel, id est, Josue obediendo in omnibus his quæ sibi Moyses commisit aut jussit, meruit esse et factus est successor Moysis in regimine Israelitici populi, quemadmodum scriptum est in Numeris: Dixit Dominus ad Moysen: Tolle Josue, virum in quo est spiritus Dei, et pone manum tuam super eum, et dabis ei partem gloriæ tuæ, ut audiat eum omnis synagoga filiorum Israel.
paras.en: [[2:55|Jesus, whilst he fulfilled the word|Jesus dum implevit verbum]], [[2:55|was made ruler in Israel|factus est dux Israel]], that is, Josue, by obeying in all the things that Moses committed to him or commanded, deserved to be, and was made, the successor of Moses in the government of the people of Israel, as is written in Numbers: [[Num 27:18|And the Lord said to him: take Josue the son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and put thy hand upon him|Dixit Dominus ad Moysen: Tolle Josue, virum in quo est spiritus Dei, et pone manum tuam super eum]], and [[Num 27:20|thou shalt give him|dabis ei]] [[Num 27:20|part of thy glory, that all the congregation of the children of Israel may hear him|partem gloriæ tuæ, ut audiat eum omnis synagoga filiorum Israel]].

paras.t: Caleb dum testificatur in ecclesia, id est, testando coram multitudine filiorum Israel, bonam et fertilem esse terram promissionis, et filios Israel eam posse faciliter obtinere Deo juvante, accepit hæreditatem, id est promissionem a Deo, quod hæreditatem consequeretur in terra promissa: quod qualiter actum sit et impletum, in Numerorum et Josue libris recitatur.
paras.en: [[2:56|Caleb, for bearing witness before the congregation|Caleb dum testificatur in ecclesia]], that is, by testifying before the multitude of the children of Israel that the land of promise was good and fertile, and that the children of Israel could easily win it with God's help, [[2:56|received an inheritance|accepit hæreditatem]], that is, the promise from God that he would obtain an inheritance in the promised land: how this was done and fulfilled is told in the books of Numbers[[Num 14:30||]][[Num 14:38||]] and Josue[[Jos 14:6||]].

paras.t: David in sua misericordia, id est merito suæ pietatis, quam in multis, præsertim in inimicissimo sibi Saule sæpe monstravit: quia nec tunc voluit, nec permisit eum occidi, quando quærebatur ab ipso Saule ad occidendum. Unde legitur primo Regum libro: Dixit David ad Abisai: Ne interficias eum; quis enim extendet manum suam in christum Domini, et innocens erit? Consecutus est sedem regni.
paras.en: [[2:57|David, by his mercy|David in sua misericordia]], that is, by the merit of his kindness, which he often showed in many things, and above all toward Saul, his bitterest enemy: for he neither willed nor allowed him to be slain even at the time when he was being sought by that same Saul to be slain. Hence it is read in the first book of Kings: [[1 Kings 26:9|And David said to Abisai: Kill him not: for who shall put forth his hand against the Lord's anointed, and shall be guiltless?|Dixit David ad Abisai: Ne interficias eum; quis enim extendet manum suam in christum Domini, et innocens erit]] He [[2:57|obtained the throne|Consecutus est sedem regni]] of the kingdom.

paras.t: Elias dum zelat, id est, amat et implet, zelum legis, id est affectum quem habuit pro legis ac divinæ majestatis honore: ob quam causam restitit Achab regi, et prophetas Baal occidit, quinquagenariosque cœlesti igne procuravit comburi; receptus est in cælum, id est, in cælum aerium meruit elevari, atque in curru igneo ad paradisum transferri, prout quarto Regum libro describitur.
paras.en: [[2:58|Elias, while he is full of zeal|Elias dum zelat]], that is, while he loves and fulfils it, [[2:58|for the law|zelum legis]] [the Latin is *zelat zelum legis*, he is zealous with the zeal of the law], that is, the affection he had for the honour of the law and of the divine majesty: for which cause he withstood king Achab, and slew the prophets of Baal[[3 Kings 18:40||]], and had the captains of fifty burnt up with fire from heaven[[4 Kings 1:10||]][[4 Kings 1:12||]]; [[2:58|was taken up into heaven|receptus est in cælum]], that is, deserved to be lifted up into the heaven of the air, and to be carried in a fiery chariot to paradise, as is described in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 2:11||]] [the margin gives IV Reg. ii].

paras.t: Ananias, Azarias, Misael credentes perfecte in Deum, liberati sunt de flamma, hoc est, in medio fornacis ardentissimæ manserunt, et inde exierunt illæsi. Propter quod Nabuchodonosor dixit: Benedictus Deus eorum, qui misit angelum suum, et eruit servos suos, qui crediderunt in eum: prout in Daniele scriptum est.
paras.en: [[2:59|Ananias and Azarias and Misael, by believing|Ananias, Azarias, Misael credentes]] perfectly in God, [[2:59|were delivered out of the flame|liberati sunt de flamma]], that is, they remained in the midst of the fiercely burning furnace, and came out of it unharmed[[Dan 3:21||]]. Wherefore Nabuchodonosor said: [[Dan 3:95|Blessed be the God of them|Benedictus Deus eorum]], [[Dan 3:95|who hath sent his angel, and delivered his servants that believed in him|qui misit angelum suum, et eruit servos suos, qui crediderunt in eum]]: as is written in Daniel.

paras.t: Daniel in sua simplicitate columbina, qua in omnibus Deum sinceriter coluit, nec adulantibus, nec comminantibus cessit, liberatus est de ore leonum, secundum quod ipse ait in libro suo Dario regi: Deus meus misit angelum, et conclusit ora leonum, et non nocuerunt mihi. Quod miraculum etiam secundo contigit Danieli sub Cyro rege, ut Danielis quartodecimo est scriptum.
paras.en: [[2:60|Daniel, in his innocency|Daniel in sua simplicitate]] [the Latin is *simplicity*], a simplicity like the dove's, by which he worshipped God sincerely in all things and gave way neither to flatterers nor to threateners, [[2:60|was delivered out of the mouth of the lions|liberatus est de ore leonum]], according to what he himself says to king Darius in his book: [[Dan 6:22|My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut up the mouths of the lions, and they have not hurt me|Deus meus misit angelum, et conclusit ora leonum, et non nocuerunt mihi]]. This miracle happened to Daniel a second time also, under king Cyrus, as is written in the fourteenth chapter of Daniel[[Dan 14:30||]].

paras.t: Et ita cogitate per generationem et generationem, id est, ea quæ acciderunt per generationum successiones et temporum intervalla fidelibus, ad memoriam revocate, prout in libris Moysis, Josue, Judicum, Regum, etc., continetur; quia omnes qui sperant in eum, id est, in Deum confidunt spe formata, non infirmantur, id est, non deficiunt corde, sed roborantur in Domino mente et etiam sæpe in corpore. Ideo ait Psalmista: In Domino sperans non infirmabor. Ecclesiasticus quoque asserit: Nullus speravit in Domino, et confusus est. Et rursus hortatur Propheta: Exspecta Dominum, viriliter age, et confortetur cor tuum, et sustine Dominum.
paras.en: [[2:61|And thus consider, through all generations|Et ita cogitate per generationem et generationem]], that is, call to mind the things that befell the faithful through the succession of generations and the intervals of times, as is contained in the books of Moses, Josue, Judges, Kings, etc.; [[2:61|that none that trust in him|quia omnes qui sperant in eum]], that is, who confide in God with a formed hope [that is, hope given its life by charity], [[2:61|fail in strength|non infirmantur]], that is, they do not faint in heart, but are strengthened in the Lord in mind, and often in body too. Therefore the Psalmist says: [[Ps 25:1|I have put my trust in the Lord, and shall not be weakened|In Domino sperans non infirmabor]]. Ecclesiasticus also asserts: [[Ecclus 2:11|no one hath hoped in the Lord, and hath been confounded|Nullus speravit in Domino, et confusus est]]. And again the Prophet exhorts: [[Ps 26:14|Expect the Lord, do manfully, and let thy heart take courage, and wait thou for the Lord|Exspecta Dominum, viriliter age, et confortetur cor tuum, et sustine Dominum]].

paras.t: Et a verbis peccatoris, id est ex comminationibus Antiochi, ne timueritis timore carnali immoderato: secundum quod Christus ait in Evangelio, Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt. Unde et in Isaia habetur: Quis tu ut timeas ab homine mortali, et a filio hominis qui quasi fœnum arescet? Ideo Salomon loquitur: Qui timet hominem, cito corruet. Quia gloria ejus stercus et vermis est, id est gloriatio ejus, inanis decor et apparatus, vilis est, fœtida, et cito putrescens.
paras.en: [[2:62|And fear not|ne timueritis]] [[2:62|the words of a sinful man|Et a verbis peccatoris]], that is, the threats of Antiochus, with an immoderate fleshly fear: according as Christ says in the Gospel, [[Matt 10:28|fear ye not them that kill the body|Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt]]. Hence we have in Isaias too: [[Is 51:12|who art thou, that thou shouldst be afraid of a mortal man, and of the son of man, who shall wither away like grass?|Quis tu ut timeas ab homine mortali, et a filio hominis qui quasi fœnum arescet]] Therefore Solomon says: [[Prov 29:25|He that feareth man shall quickly fall|Qui timet hominem, cito corruet]]. For [[2:62|his glory is dung and worms|gloria ejus stercus et vermis est]], that is, his boasting, his empty comeliness and display, is vile, foul, and quickly rotting.

paras.t: Hodie extollitur, et cras, id est cito post hæc, non invenietur, quia per mortem erit sublatus: juxta illud in Psalmo, Vidi impium superexaltatum, et transivi, et ecce non erat. Quia conversus est in terram suam. Hoc quidam exponunt de corporali Antiochi reversione ad terram Syriæ, ut dictum est capitulo præcedenti. Sed expositio hæc non consonat litteræ præcedenti, pro cujus causa istud inducitur. Ideo sensus est: Quia conversus est in terram suam, id est, post mortem protinus resolvetur in terram, de qua secundum corpus formatus est, juxta illud: Exibit spiritus ejus, et revertetur in terram suam. Nam et primo parenti Dominus dixit: In sudore vultus tui vesceris pane tuo, donec revertaris in terram, de qua sumptus es. Fuit autem hoc ipsum quod ait hic Mathathias, in Antiocho adimpletum, quia post paucos annos exspiravit ex ægritudine molestissima, qua de ejus corpore vermes ebulliebant, tantusque fœtor, quod nullus poterat eum ferre, ut infra secundo libro narratur. Et cogitatio ejus peribit, id est, effectu optato frustrabitur et damnationem recipiet.
paras.en: [[2:63|Today he is lifted up, and tomorrow|Hodie extollitur, et cras]], that is, soon after this, [[2:63|he shall not be found|non invenietur]], because he will be taken away by death: according to that in the Psalm, [[Ps 36:35|I have seen the wicked highly exalted|Vidi impium superexaltatum]], and [[Ps 36:36|I passed by, and lo, he was not|transivi, et ecce non erat]]. Because [[2:63|he is returned into his earth|Quia conversus est in terram suam]]. Some expound this of Antiochus's bodily return to the land of Syria, as was said in the preceding chapter. But this exposition does not agree with the words of the text just before, for whose sake this is brought in. Therefore the sense is: [[2:63|because he is returned into his earth|Quia conversus est in terram suam]], that is, after death he will forthwith be dissolved into the earth from which he was formed as to his body, according to that: [[Ps 145:4|His spirit shall go forth, and he shall return into his earth|Exibit spiritus ejus, et revertetur in terram suam]]. For the Lord also said to our first parent: [[Gen 3:19|In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread till thou return to the earth out of which thou wast taken|In sudore vultus tui vesceris pane tuo, donec revertaris in terram, de qua sumptus es]]. Now this very thing that Mathathias says here was fulfilled in Antiochus, for after a few years he breathed his last of a most loathsome sickness, in which worms swarmed out of his body, and there was such a stench that no one could bear him, as is told below in the second book[[2 Mach 9:9||]]. And [[2:63|his thought is come to nothing|cogitatio ejus peribit]] [Denis's text reads *peribit*, shall perish; a footnote in the edition gives the other reading, *periit*, which the Douay-Rheims follows], that is, it will be cheated of the effect it hoped for, and will receive damnation.

paras.t: Vos ergo, filii, confortamini, id est, vos ipsos invicem animate, et sperando in Domino robur accipite, atque pro confortatione corporis et animæ Deum fideliter invocate. Bellatoribus autem specialiter necessaria est fortitudo: quæ est virtus cardinalis, per quam homo viriliter aggreditur ardua, et in periculis mortis constanter se habet ac fortiter præliatur. Hinc Josue Dominus jussit: Ecce præcipio tibi, confortare et esto robustus valde. Et viriliter agite in lege, ita ut eam personaliter impleatis, et a populo vestro observari pro viribus faciatis; quia in ipsa gloriosi eritis, id est famosi et beati, si eam sic observaveritis.
paras.en: [[2:64|You, therefore, my sons, take courage|Vos ergo, filii, confortamini]], that is, hearten one another, and receive strength by hoping in the Lord, and call faithfully upon God for the strengthening of body and soul. Now fortitude is especially necessary for warriors: it is a cardinal virtue, by which a man manfully takes on hard things, and in the perils of death bears himself steadfastly and fights bravely. Hence the Lord commanded Josue: [[Jos 1:9|Behold I command thee, take courage, and be strong|Ecce præcipio tibi, confortare et esto robustus valde]] [Denis adds *valde*, very, from Jos 1:7]. And [[2:64|behave manfully in the law|viriliter agite in lege]], so that you fulfil it in your own persons, and make your people keep it as far as you are able; [[2:64|for by it you shall be glorious|quia in ipsa gloriosi eritis]], that is, renowned and blessed, if you keep it so.

paras.t: Et ecce Simon frater vester, scio quod vir consilii est, id est industriosus, circumspectus et prudens, ad dandum consilia bona aptus: qui et in dono consilii abundavit; ipsum audite auribus cordis et corporis, semper, omni scilicet tempore opportuno, præsertim in bellicis rebus: in quibus prudentia plus valet quam corporalis fortitudo; imo et fortitudinem, quæ est virtus, prudentia dirigit. Hinc scriptum in libro Sapientiæ: Melior est sapientia quam vires, et vir prudens magis quam fortis. Hoc Ecclesiastes plenius memorat: Melior est sapientia fortitudine. Et ipse erit vobis pater, id est loco patris, quantum ad consiliarem directionem. Siquidem ratione eminentiæ in sapientia, aliquis non immerito pater vocatur.
paras.en: [[2:65|And behold, I know that your brother Simon is a man of counsel|Et ecce Simon frater vester, scio quod vir consilii est]], that is, diligent, circumspect and prudent, apt to give good counsel: who also abounded in the gift of counsel [one of the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost]; [[2:65|give ear to him|ipsum audite]] with the ears of the heart and of the body, [[2:65|always|semper]], that is, at every fitting time, and above all in matters of war: in which prudence avails more than bodily strength; nay, prudence directs fortitude too, which is a virtue. Hence it is written in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 6:1|Wisdom is better than strength: and a wise man is better than a strong man|Melior est sapientia quam vires, et vir prudens magis quam fortis]]. Ecclesiastes records this more fully: [[Eccles 9:16|wisdom is better than strength|Melior est sapientia fortitudine]]. And [[2:65|he shall be a father to you|ipse erit vobis pater]], that is, in the place of a father, as regards direction by counsel. For by reason of eminence in wisdom a man is not undeservedly called a father.

paras.t: Et Judas Machabæus fortis viribus a juventute, id est ab exordio juventutis suæ, in qua adhuc est: imo nec ad senectutem pervenit, ut infra patebit; sit vobis princeps militiæ: quoniam aptus est stare in acie, et propriis factis alios animare; et ipse aget bellum populi, id est, principalis erit in præliis vestræ communitatis.
paras.en: [[2:66|And Judas Machabeus, who is valiant and strong from his youth up|Et Judas Machabæus fortis viribus a juventute]], that is, from the beginning of his youth, in which he still is: nay, he did not even reach old age, as will appear below[[1 Mach 9:18||]] [the margin gives I Mach. ix, 15 or 18; Judas's death is told at 1 Mach 9:18]; [[2:66|let him be the leader of your army|sit vobis princeps militiæ]]: for he is fit to stand in the battle line and to hearten others by his own deeds; [[2:66|and he shall manage the war of the people|et ipse aget bellum populi]], that is, he will be the chief in the battles of your community.

paras.t: Et adducetis ad vos omnes factores legis, id est, Judæos qui permanserunt in observantia legis, colligite et vobis associate. Nam et hi qui bene se habent in divinis, sunt melioris fiduciæ, secundum Philosophum, et magis adjuvari merentur a Domino. Propter quod secundo Paralipomenon libro Propheta ait Amasiæ regi Juda: O rex, ne egrediatur tecum exercitus Israel: non enim est Dominus cum Israel. Et vindicate vindictam populi vestri, id est, vindicando exercete zelo justitiæ debitam ultionem in adversarios vestros pro crudelitatibus et sceleribus quæ commiserunt in populum vestrum, magis autem in Deum. Retribuite retributionem, id est justam vindictam, gentibus vos impugnantibus.
paras.en: [[2:67|And you shall take to you all that observe the law|Et adducetis ad vos omnes factores legis]], that is, gather and join to yourselves the Jews who have remained in the observance of the law. For those who stand well in divine things are also of better confidence, according to the Philosopher, and deserve more to be helped by the Lord. Wherefore in the second book of Paralipomenon the Prophet says to Amasias, king of Juda: [[2 Par 25:7|O king, let not the army of Israel go out with thee, for the Lord is not with Israel|O rex, ne egrediatur tecum exercitus Israel: non enim est Dominus cum Israel]]. And [[2:67|revenge ye the wrong of your people|vindicate vindictam populi vestri]], that is, by avenging, exercise with the zeal of justice due vengeance on your adversaries for the cruelties and crimes they have committed against your people, and still more against God. [[2:68|Render|Retribuite]] [[2:68|their reward|retributionem]], that is, just vengeance, [[2:68|to the Gentiles|gentibus]] who fight against you.

paras.t: Et benedixit eos, id est, filiis suis imprecatus est bona, commendavitque eos Deo; et appositus est ad patres suos, id est defunctus, et quantum ad animam suam, adjunctus patribus suis in limbo ac Abrahæ sinu, saltem post purgatorii pœnas, si quid purgandum detulit secum. Et mortuus est centesimo et quadragesimo sexto anno, non vitæ suæ, quia non vixit tam diu, sed regni Græcorum. Unde elicitur, quod uno tantummodo anno præfuit populo in ducatu prædicto. Antiochus enim intravit Jerusalem anno centesimo et quadragesimo tertio: deinde post duos annos misit principem tributorum, qui vastavit Jerusalem, ut patuit. Tuncque surrexit, et se erexit Mathathias cum suis contra Antiochum; et obiit anno centesimo et quadragesimo sexto.
paras.en: [[2:69|And he blessed them|Et benedixit eos]], that is, he called down good things upon his sons, and commended them to God; [[2:69|and was joined to his fathers|et appositus est ad patres suos]], that is, he died, and as to his soul was joined to his fathers in limbo and Abraham's bosom, at least after the pains of purgatory, if he carried with him anything to be purged. [[2:70|And he died in the hundred and forty-sixth year|Et mortuus est centesimo et quadragesimo sexto anno]], not of his life, for he did not live so long, but of the kingdom of the Greeks. Hence it is gathered that he ruled the people in the said leadership for one year only. For Antiochus entered Jerusalem in the hundred and forty-third year[[1 Mach 1:21||]]: then after two years he sent the chief collector of tributes, who laid Jerusalem waste[[1 Mach 1:30||]], as was shown above. And then Mathathias rose up with his men and set himself against Antiochus; and he died in the hundred and forty-sixth year.

paras.t: Ex isto capitulo multipliciter informamur: principaliterque instituimur, quam cordialiter et amarissime debeamus ruinam Ecclesiæ deplorare, et pro ejus reformatione per orationes, lacrimas, abstinentias, humiliationes et corporum nostrorum afflictiones jugiter laborare; qualiter etiam principes christiani et cuncti fideles ad hoc idonei debeant adversariis fidei infatigabiliter repugnare, et esse parati ad mortem pro defensione christianæ religionis ac boni communis, atque pro viribus suis consilio et auxilio reformare collapsa. Insuper instruuntur prælati ac præsidentes, ut morti appropinquantes, solliciti sint de fructuoso regimine subditorum suorum post suam decessionem, et maxime ut virtuosi, discreti, condigni ad præsidentiam provehantur. Postremo docemur hic sanctorum patrum virtutes et exempla perpendere ac sectari, sicque confortari et sperare semper in Domino, et inordinatum timorem abjicere, et usque ad mortem zelari pro Dei honore ac communi salute.
paras.en: From this chapter we are taught in many ways. Chiefly we are instructed how heartily and how bitterly we ought to bewail the ruin of the Church, and to labour continually for its reform by prayers, tears, fasting, humiliations and afflictions of our bodies; and also how Christian princes, and all the faithful who are fit for it, ought to resist the adversaries of the faith untiringly, and be ready for death in defence of the Christian religion and of the common good, and to restore what has fallen, by counsel and help, as far as their strength allows. Further, prelates and superiors are instructed that, as they draw near to death, they should be careful for the fruitful government of their subjects after their departure, and above all that virtuous, discreet and worthy men be advanced to the office of superior. Lastly we are taught here to weigh and follow the virtues and examples of the holy fathers, and so to take courage and hope always in the Lord, to cast off inordinate fear, and to be zealous even unto death for the honour of God and the common salvation.

3.title: Elucidatio capituli tertii: Et surrexit Judas
3.title_en: Explanation of the third chapter: Then his son Judas, called Machabeus, rose up

paras.t: Recitatur hic, qualiter filii Mathathiæ exsecuti sint inclyti patris sui præcepta in bellis; et excellentia Judæ Machabæi hic declaratur. Et surrexit, id est, ad actus strenuos se erexit, Judas; et adjuvabant eum fratres sui, ac ceteri qui se conjunxerant patri ejus, et præliabantur prælium Israel cum lætitia, id est, alacriter et jucunde exercuerunt prælia pro communi bono Israeliticæ plebis. Exercuerunt enim prælia ex virtute multiplici, videlicet ex caritate Dei et proximorum, ex zelo justitiæ, ex fortitudine quæ est virtus cardinalis, atque ex latria quæ Deo cultum et cærimoniam exhibet. Signum autem virtutis est delectatio actioni annexa. Ideo quod Aristoteles quærit in Ethicis, an fortitudo habeat delectationem in actibus suis, ex isto habet responsionem.
paras.en: Here it is related how the sons of Mathathias carried out in their wars the precepts of their renowned father; and the excellence of Judas Machabeus is set forth. And [[3:1|Judas|Judas]] [[3:1|rose up|Et surrexit]], that is, roused himself to vigorous deeds; and [[3:2|all his brethren helped him|et adjuvabant eum fratres sui]], [[3:2|and all they that had joined themselves to his father|ac ceteri qui se conjunxerant patri ejus]], [[3:2|and they fought with cheerfulness the battle of Israel|et præliabantur prælium Israel cum lætitia]], that is, they waged their battles eagerly and joyfully for the common good of the Israelite people. For they waged them out of manifold virtue: namely out of charity towards God and their neighbours, out of zeal for justice, out of fortitude, which is a cardinal virtue, and out of latria [that is, the virtue of worship due to God alone], which shows God worship and ceremony. Now a sign of virtue is the delight joined to the act. Hence the question Aristotle raises in the Ethics, whether fortitude has delight in its acts, has its answer from this.

paras.t: Et dilatavit gloriam populo suo, id est, famam et jucunditatem auxit undique Israeliticæ plebi; et induit se loricam sicut gigas: imo veraciter gigas fuit, non corporis mole, sed operum strenuitate; et succinxit se arma bellica sua in præliis, et protegebat castra, id est turbas Israel, gladio suo. Similis factus est leoni in operibus suis: quia sicut leo est fortissimus bestiarum, ad nullius pavens occursum, sic ipse fuit pro tunc fortissimus virorum, nullum metuens inimicorum; et sicut catulus leonis rugiens in venatione. Nam sicut catulo leonis, seu leone bestiam insequente ut devoret eam, rugiente, bestia præ timore figit gradum, sic adversarii audito nomine hujus Judæ perterrebantur.
paras.en: [[3:3|And he got his people great honour|Et dilatavit gloriam populo suo]] [*dilatavit gloriam*, literally 'he widened the glory'], that is, he increased on every side the fame and the gladness of the Israelite people; [[3:3|and put on a breastplate as a giant|et induit se loricam sicut gigas]]: nay, he truly was a giant, not in bulk of body but in vigour of deeds; [[3:3|and girt his warlike armour about him in battles|et succinxit se arma bellica sua in præliis]], [[3:3|and protected the camp|et protegebat castra]], that is, the hosts of Israel, [[3:3|with his sword|gladio suo]]. [[3:4|In his acts he was like a lion|Similis factus est leoni in operibus suis]]: for as the [[Prov 30:30|lion, the strongest of beasts, who hath no fear of any thing he meeteth|leo est fortissimus bestiarum, ad nullius pavens occursum]], so was he at that time the strongest of men, fearing none of his enemies; [[3:4|and like a lion's whelp roaring for his prey|et sicut catulus leonis rugiens in venatione]]. For as, when a lion's whelp, or a lion pursuing a beast to devour it, roars, the beast stands stock-still for fear, so the adversaries were terrified when they heard the name of this Judas.

paras.t: Ideo subditur: Et persecutus est iniquos, et omnes succendit flammis, et repulsi sunt, id est, fugerunt præ timore, inimici ejus; et directa est salus in manu ejus, id est, liberatio et prosperitas Israeliticæ plebis expedite a Deo concessa et peracta est per fortitudinem et obsequium Judæ: qui fuit instrumentum et minister Omnipotentis, qui per ipsum Judam decrevit sic populo suo succurrere. Et exacerbabat, id est, ad amaritudinem provocabat, reges multos: quorum populos ac subditos expugnavit, videlicet Idumæos, Ammonitas, Moabitas, Philistæos, Syros ac alios, ut infra habetur; et in sæculum memoria ejus in benedictione, id est cum laude et imprecatione boni, quia qui audiunt gesta ipsius, dicunt: Benedicatur seu benedictus sit a Domino.
paras.en: Therefore it is added: [[3:5|And he pursued the wicked|Et persecutus est iniquos]], and all of them [[3:5|he burnt with fire|et omnes succendit flammis]]; and [[3:6|his enemies|inimici ejus]] [[3:6|were driven away|et repulsi sunt]], that is, fled for fear; [[3:6|and salvation prospered in his hand|et directa est salus in manu ejus]], that is, the deliverance and prosperity of the Israelite people was speedily granted by God and brought about through the fortitude and service of Judas, who was the instrument and minister of the Almighty, who had decreed to succour his people in this way through Judas himself. [[3:7|And he grieved|Et exacerbabat]] [*exacerbabat*, literally 'he embittered'], that is, provoked to bitterness, [[3:7|many kings|reges multos]], whose peoples and subjects he conquered, namely the Idumeans, Ammonites, Moabites, Philistines, Syrians and others, as is told below[[1 Mach 5:3||]]; [[3:7|and his memory is blessed for ever|et in sæculum memoria ejus in benedictione]], that is, with praise and with the wishing of good upon him, for those who hear of his deeds say: May he be blessed, or, Blessed be he by the Lord.

paras.t: Et perambulavit civitates Juda, et perdidit impios ex eis, et avertit iram ab Israel, id est, Israeliticum populum liberavit a tribulationibus, quas diu sustinuit ab infidelibus ex ira illorum contra ipsum, vel ex ira Dei propter vitia populi, quem reduxit ad Dei devotum obsequium. Et nominatus est usque ad novissimum terræ, id est undique valde longe ac late, ut sit hyperbolica locutio: et potuit esse quod usque ad quosdam fines terræ habitabilis devenerit fama ejus, sicut et fama Herculis; et congregavit pereuntes, id est Judæos qui a gentilibus opprimebantur, et per timorem atque supplicia ad gentilitatis facinora trahebantur.
paras.en: [[3:8|And he went through the cities of Juda|Et perambulavit civitates Juda]], [[3:8|and destroyed the wicked out of them|et perdidit impios ex eis]], [[3:8|and turned away wrath from Israel|et avertit iram ab Israel]], that is, he delivered the Israelite people from the tribulations it had long endured from the unbelievers, out of their wrath against it, or out of the wrath of God on account of the sins of the people, whom he brought back to the devout service of God. [[3:9|And he was renowned even to the utmost part of the earth|Et nominatus est usque ad novissimum terræ]], that is, everywhere, very far and wide, so that it is a hyperbolical way of speaking; though it may also be that his fame reached to some of the bounds of the habitable earth, as did the fame of Hercules; [[3:9|and he gathered them that were perishing|et congregavit pereuntes]], that is, the Jews who were oppressed by the Gentiles and were being drawn by fear and torments into the crimes of heathenism.

paras.t: Et congregavit Apollonius gentes. Apollonius iste fuit unus de principibus Antiochi, duxque Samariæ: ad quod insinuandum subjungitur, et a Samaria virtutem multam et fortem, id est copiosum et robustum exercitum. Et cognovit Judas ex revelatione quorumdam, forsitan Israelitarum in Samaria commorantium, vel exploratorum suorum; et exiit obviam illi, antequam introiret Judæam, et occidit eum. Et gladium Apollonii abstulit ab occiso: quem exuit armis, secundum Josephum, sicut David ensem Goliath; et erat pugnans in eo, id est cum gladio illo, omnibus diebus quibus pugnavit: quo constat quod fuit gladius valde valens.
paras.en: [[3:10|And Apollonius gathered together the Gentiles|Et congregavit Apollonius gentes]]. This Apollonius was one of the princes of Antiochus, and governor of Samaria: to convey which it is added, [[3:10|and a numerous and great army from Samaria|et a Samaria virtutem multam et fortem]] [*virtutem*, literally 'strength'], that is, a large and sturdy army. [[3:11|And Judas understood it|Et cognovit Judas]] from what certain persons disclosed to him, perhaps Israelites living in Samaria, or his own scouts; [[3:11|and went forth to meet him|et exiit obviam illi]] before he could enter Judea, [[3:11|and killed him|et occidit eum]]. And from the slain man [[3:12|Judas took the sword of Apollonius|Et gladium Apollonii abstulit]]: he stripped him of his arms, according to Josephus, as David took Goliath's sword[[1 Kings 17:51||]]; [[3:12|and fought with it|et erat pugnans in eo]], that is, with that sword, [[3:12|all his lifetime|omnibus diebus]], as long as he fought: from which it is clear that it was a very good sword.

paras.t: Consequenter describitur aliud bellum. Et audivit Seron princeps exercitus Syriæ inferioris, quod congregavit Judas congregationem fidelium, et ecclesiam secum, et ait: Faciam mihi nomen, id est celebrem famam, et glorificabor in regno toto Antiochi, et debellabo Judam. Ecce ambitio magna et præsumptio stulta: ideo Deus qui resistit superbis, prostravit impium illum per electum pugilem suum Judam. Et præparavit se; et ascenderunt cum eo, id est cum Seron, castra, id est turbæ armatæ, impiorum: inter quos (ut fertur) fuerunt multi transgressores perfidique Judæi a Juda expulsi. Et exivit Judas obviam illis cum paucis, Deo sic disponente, ut victoria Judæ gloriosior fieret, et a Deo concessa evidenter agnosceretur. Ut viderunt autem pauci qui erant cum Juda, exercitum adversariorum venientem obviam eis, esse magnum et fortem, dixerunt Judæ ex humano timore: Quomodo poterimus pauci pugnare ad, id est contra, multitudinem tantam tam fortem?
paras.en: Next another battle is described. [[3:13|And Seron, captain of the army of Syria, heard|Et audivit Seron princeps exercitus Syriæ inferioris]] [Denis reads *Syriæ inferioris*, 'of Lower Syria'] [[3:13|that Judas had assembled a company of the faithful, and a congregation with him|quod congregavit Judas congregationem fidelium, et ecclesiam secum]], and [[3:14|he said I will get me a name|et ait: Faciam mihi nomen]], that is, a renowned fame, [[3:14|and will be glorified in the kingdom|et glorificabor in regno]], the whole kingdom of Antiochus, [[3:14|and will overthrow Judas|et debellabo Judam]]. Behold great ambition and foolish presumption: therefore God, who [[Jas 4:6|resisteth the proud|resistit superbis]], laid that impious man low by his chosen champion Judas. [[3:15|And he made himself ready|Et præparavit se]]; and there [[3:15|went up with him|et ascenderunt cum eo]], that is, with Seron, [[3:15|the host|castra]] [*castra*, literally 'camp'], that is, the armed bands, [[3:15|of the wicked|impiorum]]: among whom (as is said) were many transgressors and faithless Jews driven out by Judas. [[3:16|And Judas went forth to meet him, with a small company|Et exivit Judas obviam illis cum paucis]], God so disposing it, that the victory of Judas might be the more glorious, and be plainly acknowledged as granted by God. [[3:17|But when they saw|Ut viderunt autem]], that is, the few who were with Judas, that [[3:17|the army coming to meet them|exercitum adversariorum venientem obviam eis]] of their adversaries was great and strong, [[3:17|they said to Judas|dixerunt Judæ]] out of human fear: [[3:17|How shall we, being few, be able to fight|Quomodo poterimus pauci pugnare]] *ad*, that is, against [Denis's text has *ad*, usually 'to', where the Vulgate has *contra*, 'against'], [[3:17|so great a multitude, and so strong|multitudinem tantam tam fortem]]?

paras.t: Et ait Judas: Facile est concludi, id est comprehendi et vinci, multos in manu, id est per manum et operationem seu potestatem, paucorum: et hoc, Deo auxiliante, sicut subjungitur. Et non est differentia in conspectu Dei liberare in multis et in paucis, id est, Deo omnipotenti æque facile est adversarios expugnare per paucos ab ipso adjutos, et per multos tales; quia non in multitudine exercitus victoria belli consistit tantum aut principaliter: quia divinæ providentiæ cuncta subduntur, et Deus secundum censuram sapientiæ atque justitiæ suæ, largitur nunc isti, nunc illi victoriam, et frequenter ex occultissimis causis seu meritis, et ipse ad libitum suum corda bellantium immutat, confortat, debilitat, confundit, obstupefacit, afficit, ordinat, exhilarat et contristat. Hinc primo Regum libro bonus et magnanimus ille Jonathas ait: Non est Domino difficile salvare in multis vel in paucis. Secundo quoque Paralipomenon libro Asa rex loquitur Deo: Domine, non est apud te ulla distantia, utrum in paucis auxilieris, an in pluribus. Et nisi ista pensentur, quasi incredibiles essent multæ historiæ Scripturarum de vario et inopinato eventu bellorum. Si autem hæc perpendantur, absque dubitatione creduntur. Hinc subditur: sed de cœlo fortitudo est, id est, potestatem prævalendi atque victoriam Deus qui in cœlo esse et habitare asseritur, præstat, juxta illud Proverbiorum: Equus paratur ad diem belli, Dominus autem salutem tribuet.
paras.en: [[3:18|And Judas said|Et ait Judas]]: [[3:18|It is an easy matter for many to be shut up|Facile est concludi]], that is, to be caught and overcome, [[3:18|in the hands|in manu]], that is, by the hand and the working or power, [[3:18|of a few|paucorum]]: and this with God's help, as is added. [[3:18|And there is no difference in the sight of the God of heaven to deliver|Et non est differentia in conspectu Dei liberare]] [[3:18|with a great multitude, or with a small company|in multis et in paucis]], that is, it is equally easy for Almighty God to overcome adversaries by a few whom he helps and by many such; for [[3:19|the success of war is not in the multitude of the army|non in multitudine exercitus victoria belli]] alone or chiefly: for all things are subject to divine providence, and God, by the judgement of his wisdom and justice, grants the victory now to this side, now to that, and often for most hidden causes or deserts; and at his pleasure he himself changes, strengthens, weakens, confounds, astounds, moves, orders, gladdens and saddens the hearts of those who fight. Hence in the first book of Kings that good and great-hearted Jonathas says: [[1 Kings 14:6|it is easy for the Lord to save either by many, or by few|Non est Domino difficile salvare in multis vel in paucis]]. In the second book of Paralipomenon, too, king Asa says to God: [[2 Par 14:11|Lord, there is no difference with thee, whether thou help with few, or with many|Domine, non est apud te ulla distantia, utrum in paucis auxilieris, an in pluribus]]. And unless these things are weighed, many histories of the Scriptures about the varied and unexpected outcome of battles would seem as it were incredible; but if they are weighed, they are believed without doubting. Hence it is added: [[3:19|but strength cometh from heaven|sed de cœlo fortitudo est]], that is, God, who is said to be and to dwell in heaven, grants the power to prevail and the victory, according to that of Proverbs: [[Prov 21:31|The horse is prepared for the day of battle: but the Lord giveth safety|Equus paratur ad diem belli, Dominus autem salutem tribuet]].

paras.t: Ipsi veniunt ad nos in multitudine contumaci, quia de viribus suis præsumunt, nosque despiciunt. Nos autem pugnabimus pro animabus nostris et legibus nostris, id est pro defensione vitæ nostræ, ac legum seu institutionum nostrarum. Lex etenim Moysis, fuit lex una aggregative continens plures leges, id est jussiones particulares. Unde per Moysen Dominus dixit: Leges meas custodite. Et Dominus conteret, id est dejiciet, eos. Hoc fuit verbum bonæ spei, imo ex divina inspiratione prolatum. Vos autem ne timueritis eos.
paras.en: [[3:20|They come against us with an insolent multitude|Ipsi veniunt ad nos in multitudine contumaci]], because they presume on their own strength and despise us. [[3:21|But we will fight for our lives, and our laws|Nos autem pugnabimus pro animabus nostris et legibus nostris]], that is, for the defence of our life and of our laws or institutions. For the law of Moses was one law containing, taken all together, many laws, that is, particular commands. Hence the Lord said through Moses: [[Lev 19:19|Keep ye my laws|Leges meas custodite]][[Lev 18:5||]]. [[3:22|And the Lord himself will overthrow them|Et Dominus conteret]], that is, will cast them down. This was a word of good hope, nay, one uttered by divine inspiration. But [[3:22|as for you, fear them not|Vos autem ne timueritis eos]].

paras.t: Ut cessavit autem loqui, insiluit in eos subito, ex impulsu divino: sicut in libro Judicum de ipsis virtuosis judicibus sæpius legitur, quod irruit in eos, seu factus est in eis Spiritus Domini, sicque fecerunt hoc aut illud. Et contritus, id est destructus, dissipatus, victus, est Seron et exercitus ejus, et ceciderunt ex eis octingenti viri. Refert Josephus, quod Judas occidit ipsum Seron ducem Syrorum et octo millia. Et de præliis Judæ narrabant omnes gentes, id est quædam de omnibus, vel omnes in circuitu Juda morantes.
paras.en: [[3:23|And as soon as he had made an end of speaking|Ut cessavit autem loqui]], [[3:23|he rushed suddenly upon them|insiluit in eos subito]] by a divine impulse: as we often read in the book of Judges of those virtuous judges, that the Spirit of the Lord rushed upon them[[Judg 14:6||]][[Judg 14:19||]][[Judg 15:14||]], or came upon them[[Judg 11:29||]], and so they did this or that. And there [[3:23|were overthrown|Et contritus]], that is, destroyed, scattered, conquered, [[3:23|Seron, and his host|est Seron et exercitus ejus]], [[3:24|and there fell of them eight hundred men|et ceciderunt ex eis octingenti viri]]. Josephus relates that Judas killed Seron himself, the general of the Syrians, and eight thousand. [[3:26|And all nations told of the battles of Judas|Et de præliis Judæ narrabant omnes gentes]], that is, some of all nations, or all who dwelt round about Juda.

paras.t: Ut audivit autem Antiochus rex sermones istos, iratus est animo, quod Judæi, quos pro nihilo reputavit, et sine resistentia ad libitum tribulavit, ita prævaluerunt principibus et exercitibus suis; et congregavit exercitum universi regni sui, volens Judæos funditus exstirpare; et aperuit ærarium suum, id est locum thesauri. Et vidit quod defecit pecunia de thesauris suis, id est in repositoriis thesaurorum, vel pecunia sumpta de thesauris suis, et tributa regionis modica, id est, quod regiones sibi subjectæ solverent sibi parva tributa: quoniam oderant eum, et paulatim rebellabant, eo quod abstulit eis leges eorum, et cultum deorum suorum. Unde subjungitur: propter dissensionem et plagam quam fecit in terra, ut tolleret legitima quæ erant a primis diebus, id est ab antiquo, quo diversæ gentes deos suos colere inceperunt. Et timuit ne non haberet sicut semel et bis, in sumptus, id est, ne non haberet facultatem dandi exercitui sufficientia stipendia pro expensis, sicut antea sæpius dedit.
paras.en: [[3:27|Now when king Antiochus heard these words, he was angry in his mind|Ut audivit autem Antiochus rex sermones istos, iratus est animo]], that the Jews, whom he had reckoned as nothing and had harried at his pleasure without resistance, had so prevailed over his princes and his armies; [[3:27|and gathered the forces of all his kingdom|et congregavit exercitum universi regni sui]], meaning to root out the Jews utterly; and [[3:28|he opened his treasury|et aperuit ærarium suum]], that is, the place of the treasure. [[3:29|And he perceived that the money of his treasures failed|Et vidit quod defecit pecunia de thesauris suis]], that is, in the storehouses of the treasures, or the money taken from his treasures, [[3:29|and that the tributes of the country were small|et tributa regionis modica]], that is, that the regions subject to him paid him small tributes: because they hated him, and were little by little rebelling, since he had taken from them their laws and the worship of their gods. Hence it is added: [[3:29|because of the dissension, and the evil that he had brought upon the land, that he might take away the laws of old times|propter dissensionem et plagam quam fecit in terra, ut tolleret legitima quæ erant a primis diebus]], that is, from of old, from when the various nations began to worship their gods. [[3:30|And he feared that he should not have as formerly enough for charges|Et timuit ne non haberet sicut semel et bis, in sumptus]] [*sicut semel et bis*, literally 'as once and twice'], that is, lest he should not have the means of giving the army sufficient pay for its expenses, as he had often given before.

paras.t: Et consternatus, id est deficiens et dejectus, animo erat valde, et cogitavit ire in Persidem ad colligendum ibi tributa regionum sibi tributariarum. Erat enim terra plurimum opulenta, præsertim in argento et auro, sicut ex libris Esther et Esdræ colligitur. Et reliquit Lysiam hominem nobilem de genere regali, qui infra vocatur cognatus regis, videlicet filii hujus Antiochi: ex quo elicitur, quod fuit cognatus Antiochi hujus aut suæ uxoris; super negotia regia, ut esset quasi vicarius regis in regimine regni et negotiorum ad regem spectantium. Et exiit Antiochus ab Antiochia civitate regni sui, urbe metropolitana, videlicet Syriæ: cujus ante metropolis fuit Damascus, juxta illud Isaiæ, Caput Syriæ Damascus. Denique, urbs illa tempore Antiochi et ante vocabatur Emath, sicque vocatur in Zacharia propheta: quam Antiochus reparans, a nomine suo Antiochiam appellavit; quæ antea vocabatur et Reblatha, ut quarto Regum libro, quo legitur quod Chaldæi adduxerunt Sedeciam regem ad regem Babylonis in Reblatha. Anno centesimo quadragesimo septimo regni Græcorum, etc., sicut expositum est, hoc est undecimo anno regni Antiochi: qui (ut supra habetur) cœpit regnare anno centesimo tricesimo septimo regni Græcorum monarchici, secundum sensum præhabitum.
paras.en: [[3:31|And he was greatly perplexed|Et consternatus]], that is, failing and cast down, [[3:31|in mind|animo erat valde]], [[3:31|and purposed to go into Persia|et cogitavit ire in Persidem]], to collect there the tributes of the regions that paid him tribute. For it was an exceedingly rich land, especially in silver and gold, as may be gathered from the books of Esther and Esdras. [[3:32|And he left Lysias, a nobleman of the blood royal|Et reliquit Lysiam hominem nobilem de genere regali]], who is called below [[2 Mach 11:35|the king's cousin|cognatus regis]], that is, of the son of this Antiochus: from which it is gathered that he was a kinsman of this Antiochus or of his wife; [[3:32|to oversee the affairs of the kingdom|super negotia regia]], so as to be as it were the king's vicar in ruling the kingdom and the affairs that belonged to the king. And Antiochus [[3:37|went forth from Antioch, the chief city of his kingdom|Et exiit Antiochus ab Antiochia civitate regni sui]], the metropolitan city, that is, of Syria, whose metropolis before was Damascus, according to that of Isaias: [[Is 7:8|the head of Syria is Damascus|Caput Syriæ Damascus]]. Further, that city in the time of Antiochus and before was called Emath, and so it is called in the prophet Zacharias[[Zach 9:2||]]; Antiochus rebuilt it and called it Antioch after his own name; earlier it was also called Reblatha, as in the fourth book of Kings, where we read that the Chaldeans brought king Sedecias [[4 Kings 25:6|to the king of Babylon, to Reblatha|ad regem Babylonis in Reblatha]]. [[3:37|in the hundred and forty-seventh year|Anno centesimo quadragesimo septimo]] of the kingdom of the Greeks, etc., as has been explained, that is, in the eleventh year of the reign of Antiochus, who (as was said above) began to reign in the hundred and thirty-seventh year of the monarchy of the kingdom of the Greeks[[1 Mach 1:11||]], in the sense given before.

paras.t: Et vidit Judas et fratres ejus, quod multiplicata sunt mala, id est adversa atque pericula eis imminentia, scilicet quod exercitus adversariorum a Lysia missus, copiosus, robustus, et expertissimos duces in rebus bellicis habens, quorum unus fuit Gorgias, qui libro secundo dicitur in talibus fuisse expertissimus, appropinquaret ad eos, sicut subjungitur: et exercitus Syrorum applicabat ad fines eorum. Et cognoverunt Judas et sui verba regis Antiochi, quæ mandavit populo nostro videlicet facere in interitum et consummationem, id est Judæos omnes occidere, et prorsus de terra auferre: sicque quod dicitur, Populo, posset referri ad verba ista sequentia, quod scilicet jussit populo Judæorum inferri interitum et eradicationem finalem. Et dixerunt unusquisque Judæorum cum Juda exsistentium, ad proximum suum, animando se invicem: Erigamus dejectionem populi nostri, id est, ruinam et oppressionem plebis nostræ recuperemus, resistendo adversariis, quatenus plebs nostra dudum dejecta et hostibus subdita, jam eis prævaleat, et pugnemus pro populo nostro et pro sanctis nostris, id est pro conservatione legum nostrarum et sacrorum locorum ac solennitatum. Et congregatus est conventus Judæorum ad Judam ex diversis urbibus Judææ, ut essent parati ad prælium, imo ad omnia necessaria et accommoda ad victoriam obtinendam, et quæ Judas eis præciperet, et ut orarent, et peterent misericordiam, id est pietatem gratiæ Dei, et miserationes, id est multiplices divinæ pietatis effectus contra diversas miserias eis inexsistentes aut imminentes.
paras.en: [[3:42|And Judas, and his brethren, saw that evils were multiplied|Et vidit Judas et fratres ejus, quod multiplicata sunt mala]], that is, adversities and dangers hanging over them: namely that the army of their adversaries sent by Lysias, numerous, strong, and having commanders most expert in matters of war, one of whom was Gorgias, who in the second book is said to have been most expert in such things[[2 Mach 8:9||]], was drawing near to them, as is added: [[3:42|and that the armies approached to their borders|et exercitus Syrorum applicabat ad fines eorum]]. [[3:42|And they knew|Et cognoverunt]], Judas and his men, [[3:42|the orders the king had given|verba regis]] Antiochus, [[3:42|to destroy the people, and utterly abolish them|quæ mandavit populo nostro videlicet facere in interitum et consummationem]] [literally 'which he commanded our people, namely, to bring to destruction and consummation'], that is, to kill all the Jews and take them utterly from the earth: and so the word *populo*, 'to the people', could be referred to the words that follow it [that is, read not as those to whom the order was given but as those to whom the destruction was to be done], namely that he commanded destruction and final uprooting to be brought upon the people of the Jews. [[3:43|And they said, every man|Et dixerunt unusquisque]] of the Jews who were with Judas, [[3:43|to his neighbour|ad proximum suum]], encouraging one another: [[3:43|Let us raise up the low condition of our people|Erigamus dejectionem populi nostri]], that is, let us repair the ruin and oppression of our people by resisting our adversaries, so that our people, long cast down and subject to its enemies, may now prevail over them, [[3:43|and let us fight for our people, and our sanctuary|et pugnemus pro populo nostro et pro sanctis nostris]], that is, for the preservation of our laws, and of the holy places and solemnities. [[3:44|And the assembly was gathered|Et congregatus est conventus]] of the Jews to Judas from the various cities of Judea, [[3:44|that they might be ready for battle|ut essent parati ad prælium]], nay, for everything needful and fitting for gaining the victory, and for whatever Judas should command them, [[3:44|and that they might pray, and ask mercy|et ut orarent, et peterent misericordiam]], that is, the loving-kindness of God's grace, [[3:44|and compassion|et miserationes]], that is, the manifold effects of the divine loving-kindness against the various miseries that were upon them or hanging over them.

paras.t: Et Jerusalem non habitabatur, sed erat sicut desertum; et sanctum, id est locus templi seu ipsum templum, conculcabatur a pessimis et crudelissimis gentilibus prope templum morantibus, et circa templum seu per illud discurrentibus. De quibus subjungitur: et filii alienigenarum erant in arce; et ablata est voluptas a Jacob, id est a Judæis ex Jacob natis ablata est multiplex lætitia, quam consuebant habere in solennitatibus, in quibus confluebant ad templum, præcipue ter in anno, atque in sacrificiis quæ fiebant in templo; et defecit ibi tibia et cithara, id est musica instrumenta, quibus in officiis Dei ex devotione utebantur: imo cum instrumentis talibus et melodiis eorum solebant venire ad templum seu sacrificii locum, prout primo Regum libro patet.
paras.en: [[3:45|Now Jerusalem was not inhabited, but was like a desert|Et Jerusalem non habitabatur, sed erat sicut desertum]]; [[3:45|and the sanctuary|et sanctum]], that is, the place of the temple or the temple itself, [[3:45|was trodden down|conculcabatur]] by the most wicked and cruel Gentiles, who lived near the temple and ran about round the temple or through it. Of whom it is added: [[3:45|and the children of strangers were in the castle|et filii alienigenarum erant in arce]]; [[3:45|and joy was taken away from Jacob|et ablata est voluptas a Jacob]], that is, from the Jews born of Jacob was taken away the manifold gladness they used to have in the solemnities, when they flocked to the temple, chiefly three times a year, and in the sacrifices that were offered in the temple; [[3:45|and the pipe and harp ceased there|et defecit ibi tibia et cithara]], that is, the musical instruments which they used out of devotion in the offices of God: nay, with such instruments and their melodies they used to come to the temple or the place of sacrifice, as is clear from the first book of Kings[[1 Kings 10:5||]].

paras.t: Et venerunt in Maspha, id est oppidum Judææ sic nuncupatum, contra Jerusalem, id est ex opposito: quatenus ab illo loco dirigerent facies suas versus templum in sua oratione, prout tertio libro Regum agendum esse innuitur ab his, qui ad templum venire non poterant; quemadmodum etiam Daniel se fecisse testatur, quum esset cum Dario rege; quia locus orationis erat in Maspha ante in Israel, id est, filii Israel, templo nondum constructo, solebant convenire in Maspha ad orandum. Scriptum est enim primo libro Regum: Dixit Samuel, Congregate universum Israel in Maspha, ut orem pro vobis Dominum. In Judicum quoque libro: Locutus est Jephte omnes sermones suos coram Domino in Maspha.
paras.en: They [[3:46|came to Maspha|Et venerunt in Maspha]], that is, the town of Judea so named, [[3:46|over against Jerusalem|contra Jerusalem]], that is, facing it: so that from that place they might turn their faces towards the temple in their prayer, as the third book of Kings intimates is to be done by those who could not come to the temple[[3 Kings 8:44||]] [the margin gives only III Reg. viii; the praying towards the temple is in 8:44 and 8:48]; as Daniel too is attested to have done when he was with king Darius[[Dan 6:10||]]; [[3:46|for in Maspha was a place of prayer heretofore in Israel|quia locus orationis erat in Maspha ante in Israel]], that is, the children of Israel, before the temple was built, used to gather in Maspha to pray. For it is written in the first book of Kings: [[1 Kings 7:5|And Samuel said: Gather all Israel to Masphath, that I may pray to the Lord for you|Dixit Samuel, Congregate universum Israel in Maspha, ut orem pro vobis Dominum]]. And in the book of Judges: [[Judg 11:11|And Jephte spoke all his words before the Lord in Maspha|Locutus est Jephte omnes sermones suos coram Domino in Maspha]].

paras.t: Et jejunaverunt illa die, ad impetrandum misericordiam et miserationes. Ob quam causam fecerunt et ea quæ sequuntur: et induerunt se ciliciis, et cinerem posuerunt in capite suo, id est, capitibus suis supersparserunt, humiliando se valde, in signum mœroris, sicut de amicis suis Job loquitur: Sparserunt pulverem super caput suum in cœlum. Et destituerunt vestimenta sua, id est, in signum desolationis abjecerunt vestes valoris et alicujus jucunditatis, indueruntque lugubres vestes. Aliqui tamen exponunt, Destituerunt, id est, sciderunt.
paras.en: [[3:47|And they fasted that day|Et jejunaverunt illa die]], to obtain mercy and compassion. For the same reason they also did what follows: [[3:47|and put on haircloth|et induerunt se ciliciis]], [[3:47|and put ashes upon their heads|et cinerem posuerunt in capite suo]], that is, sprinkled them over their heads, humbling themselves greatly in sign of grief, as Job says of his friends: [[Job 2:12|they sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven|Sparserunt pulverem super caput suum in cœlum]]. [[3:47|And they rent their garments|Et destituerunt vestimenta sua]] [Denis's text reads *destituerunt*, 'they put off'; the margin gives the other readings *disciderunt*, 'they rent', and *dissuerunt*, 'they unstitched'], that is, in sign of desolation they cast off their garments of value and of any comeliness, and put on garments of mourning. Some, however, explain *destituerunt* as 'they rent'.

paras.t: Et expanderunt libros legis: forsitan ad legendum aliqua capitula ex eis pro populo confortando; vel, ut aliqui dicunt, in signum quod parati erant se morti exponere pro lege tuenda; sive ut Deus dignaretur attendere et implere promissiones, quas in Deuteronomio repromisit zelatoribus et observatoribus legis, quod scilicet daret eis victoriam contra æmulos legis. De quibus libris scrutabantur gentes similitudinem simulacrorum suorum, id est, gentiles inquirebant comprobare culturam idolorum suorum, quia ex libris legis probabant in tabernaculo Moysis ex præcepto Dei fuisse similitudines sive imagines Cherubim, juxta illud Exodi: Duos Cherubim aureos et productiles facies ex utraque parte oraculi. Hæc autem probatio fuit inefficax, quia imagines non erant positæ ibi ut adorarentur vel colerentur, neque ut res quas repræsentabant, videlicet angelici spiritus, colerentur ut dii, sed ad designandum quod mentes illæ angelicæ jugiter Creatori adsistant ad obsequendum. Gentiles autem ista scrutantes ex lege, fuerunt eruditi, et forsan philosophi, cognoscentes esse unum summum Deum, et nihilo minus deos suos colentes. Imo quidam philosophi, ut Porphyrius, concesserunt legem Moysis esse datam a Deo, nec idololatriam esse in lege prohibitam nisi Hebræis, dicentes quod Deus altissimus voluit solus coli ab illis, non tamen voluit deos non adorari ab aliis gentibus: ad quod allegabant illud Exodi, Diis non detrahes: et illud, Si dixerit servus, Diligo dominum meum, offeret eum dominus diis. Contra quam stultam opinionem arguit Augustinus in libro de Civitate Dei.
paras.en: [[3:48|And they laid open the books of the law|Et expanderunt libros legis]]: perhaps to read some chapters from them to strengthen the people; or, as some say, in sign that they were ready to expose themselves to death in defence of the law; or that God might deign to heed and fulfil the promises he had made in Deuteronomy[[Deut 28:1||]] to those who were zealous for the law and kept it, namely that he would give them victory against the enemies of the law.
